functions.label: Shared one-rank update primitives
functions.evidence_summary: The common up/down hook 0x00B498D0 / 0x00B498F0 calls these to increment/decrement the instance field at +0x50, then refresh the level-indexed value at +0x4C through 0x0046FA80. The exact-build vtables for Immolation (0x00F277EC), Carrion Swarm (0x00F887B0), Shadow Strike (0x00F98714), and Cluster Rockets (0x00FB2C6C) point directly to these common hooks at +0x2E4 / +0x2E8. Earthquake (0x00F85CF0) uses wrappers 0x00C298D0 / 0x00C298F0, which call the common hooks and then an additional virtual slot +0x434. This is a high-value shared rank lifecycle with a visible class-specific extension point.

functions.label: Shared attached-ability disable/enable state transitions
functions.evidence_summary: Disable increments the ability instance counter at +0x3C; the first transition from zero invokes virtual +0xE0, clears instance flag bit 0x2, and invokes +0xC4. Enable decrements the same counter; a transition from positive to below one invokes +0xE4 and may restore flag bit 0x2 plus invoke +0xC8, depending on unit flag +0x164 & 4. Both paths refresh shared UI state. A secondary instance counter at +0x40 is also adjusted based on the wrapper's hideUI argument. Full-analysis Ghidra found 107 direct callers of disable and 99 of enable. In sampled exact-build vtables, Carrion Swarm (0x00F887B0), Shadow Strike (0x00F98714), and Cluster Rockets (0x00FB2C6C) use defaults at these hooks: +0xC4=0x0046A470, +0xC8=0x0046A480, +0xE0=0x0046A4A0, +0xE4=0x0046A500. Immolation (0x00F277EC) overrides +0xC4=0x00B6D6D0 and +0xE4=0x00B6D6F0; Earthquake (0x00F85CF0) overrides +0xC4=0x00C29CB0 and +0xC8=0x00C29CD0. The counters can be adjusted without a transition, so inspect callers and class hooks before assigning exact gameplay meaning to every branch.

functions.label: JASS GetUnitAbilityLevel / SetUnitAbilityLevel wrappers
functions.evidence_summary: All four level natives share a preflight check for internal tag 0x2B61676C and object field +0x20 == 0; the meaning of this gate is not yet named. They then locate the attached instance through 0x006D6570. Get returns its stored zero-based rank at object offset +0x50, plus one, or zero if no eligible instance is found. Set clamps the requested level to [1, maxLevel] using 0x0046F5C0, then repeatedly invokes virtual +0x2E4 to raise or +0x2E8 to lower rank on that same instance. It does not remove/recreate the ability. IncUnitAbilityLevel (0x00498B20) and DecUnitAbilityLevel (0x0048F150) use the same virtual hooks with max/level-one bounds.

functions.label: JASS UnitAddAbility / UnitRemoveAbility wrappers
functions.evidence_summary: Registered in the native table at 0x0049B3C0. Add resolves the unit, looks up the requested rawcode and returns false if an instance already exists, then calls factory 0x00AF3BA0 inside synchronization helpers and returns whether it created an instance. Remove resolves the unit, looks up the rawcode, removes the found instance through 0x006D8530, and returns whether it found one. Both notify through 0x005F6D00 after a successful change. These named natives provide a direct, reproducible path into shared ability ownership and teardown.

functions.label: JASS UnitDamageTarget damage-event handoff
functions.evidence_summary: Exact-build disassembly confirms the wrapper resolves source unit and target widget handles, validates attack-type, damage-type, and weapon-type indices, initializes a stack payload through 0x006A9940, then calls the target's +0x120 virtual method and returns true after dispatch. Carrion Swarm independently initializes the same payload and dispatches through the same slot. For CUnit targets that slot resolves to 0x006677C0, which performs unit-specific mitigation and life mutation. Positive UnitDamagePoint processing (0x006EB640 -> 0x006E9ED0) also dispatches through +0x120. The CUnit receiver invokes attached recipient-side handlers through +0xF8/+0xFC; verified class examples include Spirit Link group 2 and Mana Shield group 5. This establishes shared receiver infrastructure for UnitDamageTarget, UnitDamagePoint, and Carrion Swarm, while ordinary weapon-hit convergence on this payload path remains unconfirmed.

functions.label: Shared configured damage-bonus matrix lookup
functions.evidence_summary: The CUnit spell/direct-damage receiver 0x006677C0 and ordinary attack calculation 0x00B23C30 both call this helper. It lazily loads seven eight-entry Misc rows (DamageBonusSpells, Normal, Pierce, Siege, Magic, Chaos, Hero), then returns row[param2 * 8 + param3]. The installed base MiscGame.txt labels columns SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE, FORT, NORMAL, HERO, DIVINE, NONE, confirming param3 as defense class in the weapon calculation. The attack routine selects a weapon/attack type from unit attack data for param2. Its static body calls target validation and state helpers and this matrix lookup, but does not call payload initializer 0x006A9940 or receiver 0x006677C0; this negative finding applies only to attack calculation 0x00B23C30, not later impact processing. Later ordinary attack impact now establishes payload and CUnit receiver convergence for attack types 1 and 4 when no attached ability handles the event. Types 2, 3, and 5–8 schedule distinct effects, with impact convergence still open. Receiver-side param2/type derivation and behavior for the legacy table remain open; ethereal adjustments are handled separately.

functions.label: Area-unit enumeration
functions.evidence_summary: Clause-driven area-query builder/executor with caller callback and separate generated predicate lists. Phoenix Fire periodic acquisition 0x00C0ECD0 uses callback 0x00C0F1E0; Carrion Swarm update 0x00C31430 uses 0x00C31220, caps candidates at 64, then selects victims for its separate impact callback 0x00C30BB0. Generated predicates directly observed: 0x00696CF0 checks required/forbidden unit flags; 0x00696A00 requires candidate +0x20 bit 3 clear; 0x00696D20 checks candidate byte +0x37 in 0x41..0x5A and unit flag +0x164 bit 0x40000000 clear; 0x00696DD0 checks unit flag +0x164 bit 0x10000 set and masked bits 0x8000080 != 0x80; 0x00696D80 is its inverse; 0x00696C60 returns candidate +0x454 & 0x40; 0x00696A20 compares candidate value to query +0x14; 0x006967E0 tests candidate virtual +0xEC against query mask +0x0C; 0x00696DB0 compares candidate +0x34 to query +0x2C; 0x00696BE0 rejects when 0x006ADB90(candidate, query+0x3C, query+0x40, query+0x44) is nonzero; 0x00696AB0 performs lookup from candidate +0x34 and compares result +0x1C0 with query +0x30, or requires query value zero on lookup failure. 0x00696370 is a closest-candidate accumulator. Field and flag meanings remain unmapped. Candidates pass generated predicates before the caller callback; callback result zero stops processing. functions.label: CAbilityAttack target-mask and relation validation
functions.evidence_summary: Exact-build callers 0x00B1EC60 and 0x00B1EF60 are CAbilityAttack target-selection routines; both examine two authored target slots, expand masks through 0x006AEA70, call this validator, treat return 0 as a match, and aggregate nonzero results as rejection codes. On success they write the selected slot index; 0xFFFFFFFF indicates no slot selected. Ordinary weapon attack calculation 0x00B23C30 calls 0x00B1EC60, and common order/attack helpers also reach both selector functions. The validator rejects malformed or empty masks, intersects the expanded mask with normalized candidate target flags, emits distinct codes for target-category mismatches, then delegates self/owner and player-relation checks to 0x006AD670. That helper compares owner indices, supports a self-target case, and queries two player-relation bitsets through 0x00478DA0 and 0x0047FAA0; flag bits selectively allow failed checks. The two relation branches specifically test passive alliance (type 0) and shared spells (type 4), identified from GetPlayerAlliance table indexing and Retail common.j. Rejection-code text remains unmapped. The higher-level gate 0x006ADB90 supplies unit state, relation, and visibility checks before invoking it. Numeric mask bit meanings and each returned code’s JASS/UI text remain unmapped.

The receiver calls 0x006A0630, computes an adjusted amount, then invokes its +0x128 method (0x00668DB0) with the negative amount and returns the resulting value through an output pointer.
